author: Emma Grunwald Sun staff writer
title: Operation Fresh Start to feature authors at 'Sip & Sign' fundraising event | Daily-news-alerts | thewesterlysun.com
text:
STONINGTON — A local nonprofit aiming to help families and children in need will host its annual “Sip & Sign” fundraiser with various authors later this month to raise money for its annual fund in support of its Christmas, backpack and pajama drives.
Pawcatuck-based organization Operation Fresh Start Inc. was founded in 2020 to serve families with children in crisis in southeastern Connecticut. The all-volunteer 501(c)(3) non-profit has assisted hundreds of local families in need of making safe and thriving homes.
The organization was started by Pawcatuck resident Shannon DePerry in the basement of her home in 2020, where she gave out suitcases filled with necessities for young people aging out of the foster care system.
"I started a luggage drive back in 2020 for kids in foster care, and it turned into 600 suitcases, 350 toiletry bags. Not my plan, but that's what happened," DePerry said in an interview.
Demand grew during COVID, and the service expanded to include moms, dads, children who have known economic hardship, domestic violence, or people recovering from other challenges.
DePerry said the organization now raises about $35,000 to $40,000 each year and estimated that it has helped more than 1,000 families since it began.
Services include providing welcome baskets for families transitioning out of homelessness, such as trash cans, cleaning supplies, kitchen towels, pot holders, and utensils.
"We find everything that they need to make a house a home," DePerry said.
DePerry, who works as a floral manager at McQuade's Marketplace, noted that the organization is completely volunteer-based. “Nobody gets paid. We all just do it from our heart,” she said.
DePerry said that local families are struggling now more than ever because of rising housing and gas costs. "It's horrendous," she said.
She described helping one family who had been homeless for four years and had just gotten an apartment. Operation Fresh Start provided them with various items for their new apartment, including an oven.
"We filled their car up, and we just gave them hope and a fresh start," DePerry said.
The nonprofit also recently held a backpack drive, where it gave out over 200 backpacks and over 3,000 individual school supplies to children, DePerry said.
The fundraising event for the organization will take place from 5 p.m. to 9 p.m. at the Stonington Free Library on Sunday, Oct. 18.
Tickets cost $45 per person and include small bites, a drink ticket, and one raffle ticket.
DePerry highlighted cocktails, appetizers, and silent auction items including an overnight stay at the Taber Inn in Mystic, designer earrings, a Michael Kors pocket book, UConn basketball game tickets, and various art pieces for people interested in attending.
"People can come out and have a really nice night for $45 and know that everything that they're giving is going back into our community," DePerry said.
She hopes to raise about $7,000 at this year's event, up from the $5,000 raised last year.
The Sip & Sign fundraiser will feature six authors, including first-time Survivor winner Richard Hatch, Kelly Jarvis, James Bennett, Monica Dilorio, George Kimmerle, MJ Soni, Marilyn Wright Dayton, Debbie McGrath, Rick Koster, and Becki Jason.
Hatch's new book "Reality Matters,” is both a memoir and a reflection on the true nature of reality in a reality TV-obsessed culture. The other authors come from several different genres, including children's literature, historical fiction, modern romance, nonfiction, and memoir.
To purchase tickets and learn more about the event, visit StoningtonFreeLibrary.org.
